about: Facts and chart data for ThrusterChain page pass 4. Read with notes/p4_facts.md. Every number here was computed by scripts/p4_facts_compute.py, p4_facts_extra.py and p4_facts_build.py (read only) or read from the named source file. Rounded for display; recompute from the scripts for full precision.

conventions.thruster_sign: Commands run from -1 to 1. Negative pushes upstream, against the water. Thruster 1's full throttle is -1. 'Past 80%' means |a| > 0.800000011920929 (the float32 knee); a command of exactly 80% does not stall.
conventions.histogram_bins: 50 bins. Signed: edges linspace(-1, 1, 51) with the edges at -0.8 and +0.8 set to -/+0.800000011920929; negative bins are [lo, hi), positive bins (lo, hi], 0 goes to bin 25 [0, 0.04]. Magnitude |a|: edges linspace(0, 1, 51) with the 0.8 edge set to the knee; bins (lo, hi], 0 goes to bin 0. So bins 0-4 (signed) and 45-49 (signed) and 40-49 (magnitude) hold exactly the commands past 80%.

verified_claims.claim: Only 60 of the 42,500 kept training rows go past 80% (main test, densest-15% removal)
verified_claims.detail: All 60 are thruster 1 pushing upstream past 80% (none of thrusters 2-4 ever goes past 80% in the data), and all 60 are the recording controller's full-throttle commands that lie outside the removed ball (0.89% of the 6,712 full-throttle commands survive).
verified_claims.source: design seed 900, regenerated with experiments/shift/dataset.generate(900) + shift.define_gap; page #shift

verified_claims.claim: 93.7% of strong-current states are in the full-throttle region
verified_claims.detail: Share of the 100,000 visited states (1,000 bank starts x 100 steps) with c + w1 > 0.565. The push does not depend on the controller, so it is the same for every controller. Recorded conditions 27.86%, big waves 39.61%, big starting pushes 27.86% (same current and waves as recorded).
verified_claims.source: truth.bank_rollout on thruster_chain.bank_starts; page #shift table column 3

verified_claims.claim: The rising-thrust controller scores -54.1 points in strong current
verified_claims.detail: Stalling world. It goes past 80% on 84.0% of the states it visits there.

Average 100-step return over the 1,000 recorded-conditions bank starts, stalling world: the recording controller (0 points) and the stall-aware controller (100 points). Recomputed: -79.7996 and -26.3600.
thrust(a) = sign(a)(0.8 - 1.5(|a| - 0.8)) past the knee; because the knee is the float32 of 0.8, the exact values are 3e-8 above the round numbers (0.65000003, 0.50000003).

verified_claims.claim: The water's push points upstream on 20.3% of big-wave states
verified_claims.detail: Push c + w1 < 0. Range over visited states -0.595 to 1.389 (page: -0.6 to 1.4). Recorded conditions: 6.13% upstream, range -0.295 to 1.089; strong current: never upstream, range 0.304 to 1.492.

verified_claims.claim: Stage 1: a penalty placed by the exact one-step error won back 93.9 of the 98.9 points lost in strong current
verified_claims.verdict: 98.9 verified; 93.9 taken from the page (raw Stage 1 outputs are not on this machine)
verified_claims.detail: The 98.9 is the return-cost check's harm in strong current at critic weight 5 (seeds 95.2-102.8). The 93.9 (seeds 83.4 to 103.9) is in the page's Stage 1 table (#beyond-the-data); its run outputs (runs/shift_explore/room/) were made in a cloud session and are not in WSL or the work folder. Precise wording: the penalty, at training states and at the actor's own command, was [delta*(s, actor's command) - delta*(s, recorded command)]+, how much more the critic's exact one-step error at the actor's command exceeds that at the recorded command, counted only when positive (outputs/shift/beyond-the-data/stage1/README.md).

recorded conditions 5.8, big starting pushes 11.8, big waves 16.6, strong current 98.9: the actor of the full-log critic minus the actor of the critic trained after the densest-15% removal, critic weight 5, mean of seeds 0-4.

verified_claims.claim: BCA's own lower-edge penalty is 1/30 to 1/160 of the perfect one and barely tracks it
verified_claims.detail: Measured at the actor's commands on training rows: BCA's width there minus its width at the recorded command, against the same penalty built from the critic's exact one-step error. 1/31-1/33 on the three lower qualities, 1/58 on medium-expert, 1/163 on expert; row-by-row correlation -0.17 to 0.29 (quality means).

verified_claims.claim: Version-5 data: no thruster-1 commands past 80% in the expert data; 3.6-9.9% in the other qualities, all random
verified_claims.verdict: partly verified: the 'none' and 'all random' parts hold; the 3.6-9.9% range does not reproduce exactly (see value)
verified_claims.detail: Expert: zero training rows past 80% on any thruster, in every seed. Other qualities, training split, thruster 1 past 80% upstream (a1 < -0.8, the direction of the hold): random 9.98-10.11%, medium-replay 8.21-8.43%, medium 6.45-6.59%, medium-expert 3.25-3.53% of rows (all rows before the removal); on the rows kept after the hold removal 3.61-3.90% (medium-expert) to 9.99-10.12% (random). About as many go past 80% downstream (a1 > +0.8). Every one of these rows is a uniform random command (infos/random = True on 100% of them). Suggested wording: 'none in the expert data; in the other qualities about 3% to 10% of training steps push thruster 1 upstream past 80%, and every one of them is a uniform random command'.

formula.throttle_cost: 0.3 a^2 per thruster, on the clipped command, in both worlds, even while stalling

thrust_and_cost.note: push minus cost is shown only as a convenience for a slider readout; push and cost are in different units of the problem (push moves the floats; the cost is subtracted from the reward), so the page should not call it a net value without saying so.

main_test_seed900_thruster1.source: design seed 900 training split (50,000 rows); kept = after the densest-15% removal (42,500 rows); removed = the 7,500 deleted rows
main_test_seed900_thruster1.note: Every past-80% command is upstream (negative). The removal deletes 6,652 of the 6,712 past-80% rows; the 60 that stay sit at |a1| 0.96-1.0.

weighting_test_expert_seed0_thruster1.source: runs/shift_iw_v5/expert/data/seed0/train_law.hdf5, training split; hold removed = rows outside truth/in_ball
weighting_test_expert_seed0_thruster1.note: The 80% hold is thruster 1 at exactly -0.800000011920929 (the knee): at 80%, not past it. The expert data hold no command past 80% at all.

four_throttle_widget.push_and_cost: see thrust_and_cost; the same function for every thruster

thrusters.1: pushes the speeds of floats 1 and 2 (observation items 1 and 3); the only thruster on float 1
thrusters.4: floats 4 and 5 (items 7 and 9); the only thruster on float 5

one_step_push_into_speeds.note: next state = A x + B thrust + water push: each thruster adds 0.3 x its push to the speed numbers of its two floats; the water adds 0.3 (c + w1) to every float's speed number

removed_ball.note: The ball is a 4-D region: a command is removed only if its distance to the centre, over all four throttles together, is at most the radius. The per-thruster intervals are its shadows, not the removal rule.

commands_on_evaluation_banks.source: bank rollouts (stalling world, 1,000 starts x 100 steps): 5th/50th/95th percentile of each thruster's command; share of states past 80% on any thruster; share with thruster 1 at its -80% limit (stall-aware); share of commands inside the main test's removed ball

observation_space.source: 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles over the 100,000 states at which a command is given (1,000 evaluation bank starts x steps 0-99) in each situation, stalling world, for the recording controller (with its fixed bank noise streams, as for the 0-point anchor) and for the stall-aware controller (the 100-point anchor). The column seed900_training_data is the main test's training split (50,000 rows), which matches the recording controller in the recorded conditions.
observation_space.names_from_env_docstring: s (10): the positions and speeds of the five floats (coordinates 2j and 2j + 1); c (1): the strength of the current, never changes during an episode; (w1, w2): the wave, a point turning 0.27 rad per step (a 23.3-step cycle), like the hands of a clock

components.name: strength of the current; never changes during an episode
components.at_rest_note: no rest value: drawn at the start; c stays fixed

components.name: wave, first number: amplitude x cos(phase), the push the wave adds now
components.at_rest_note: no rest value: drawn at the start, then turns 0.27 rad per step (amplitude fixed)

components.name: wave, second number: amplitude x sin(phase), the push it added a quarter cycle (5.8 steps) earlier
components.at_rest_note: no rest value: drawn at the start, then turns 0.27 rad per step (amplitude fixed)

observation_space.notes: c and the wave do not depend on the controller, so their ranges are the same for both controllers. The wave's range in big waves is wider (amplitude 0.4-0.7). Floats range widest in big starting pushes (start SD 1.5) and are shifted downstream (negative position numbers) in strong current.

rewards_example.note: One state, thruster 1 set to -0.8, -0.9, -1.0 (80%, 90%, 100% upstream); thrusters 2-4 at the stall-aware controller's command. The reward of this step depends only on the state and the throttle, so it is the same in both worlds; the stall shows up in the next state's float cost and in the exact value. Exact value = discounted (0.98) sum of rewards over 1,000 steps with the stall-aware controller continuing after the first step (the page's 'true value').

rest_c0.9.label: floats at rest, current 0.9 (strong current), no wave

rest_c0.6_w0.3.label: floats at rest, current 0.6, wave w1 = 0.3, w2 = 0 (inside the recorded conditions, in the full-throttle region: push 0.9)

rewards_example.recommended: rest_c0.6_w0.3 (inside the recorded conditions, in the full-throttle region)

points.formula: points = 100 (J - J_rec) / (J_top - J_rec), per situation, on the same 1,000 bank starts

difficulty.harm_source: outputs/shift/stop-report/check2_return/alpha5/pooled.json (harm = actor of the full-log critic minus actor of the critic trained after the densest-15% removal, critic weight 5, seeds 0-4)
difficulty.arms_source: outputs/shift/stop-report/README.md check 2 table; plain TD3+BC from outputs/shift/beyond-the-data/anatomy.md section 6
difficulty.note: Raw returns of the learned actors are derived from their mean points and the anchors (exact up to the 0.1-point rounding of the points). By raw return, big starting pushes is hardest for both reference controllers and for the cloned and full-log-critic actors; for the actor of the critic trained after the removal (and plain TD3+BC), strong current is lowest (-275 against -211).

weighting_test_ball.note: The weighting test also uses the densest-15% rule, on the expert's commands; the ball lands on the 80% hold (thruster 1 at -0.8 with the other three at 0.8 x the full-throttle pattern). About two thirds of the removed rows are holds; the rest are normal-driving commands near the ball's centre. The page's '99.57-99.79% of holds removed' is the design check's quadrature value; counting the training rows gives the holds_removed_training_rows values.
